To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have determined the boundaries of RyR1 monomers in a subnanometre-resolution cryo-EM map, and that we have generated three structural models for amino acids 1–565 of RyR1 that localize close to regions of the protein involved in communication with the transverse tubule voltage sensor.

we have delineated RyR1 monomeric boundaries and identified a β-sheet in the cytoplasm of RyR1 that resembles the cytoplasma pore structures of inwardly rectifying K+ channels, and we have generated a structural context for channel gating and the effects of certain malignant hyperthemia and central core disease associated mutations.
the cytoplasmically exposed regions of the RyR1 channel are composed of three structural folds that localize close to regions involved in communication with the transverse tubule voltage sensor.

understanding the structure and function of the skeletal muscle Ca2+-release channel, RyR1.
understanding the structure and function of the skeletal muscle calcium release channel (RRC).
elucidating the structure and function of the skeletal muscle Ca2+-release channel, also known as the RyR1.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, by combining cryo-EM and comparative modeling, we have been able to define the boundaries and the structural folds for a large cytoplasmic domain of RyR1.
we were able to identify the RyR1 cytoplasmic domain structure at subnanometer resolution and provide structural models of these domains that are consistent with the cryo-EM map.
we have delineated a model for the cytoplASMic domain of skeletal muscle Ca2+-release channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to identify the boundaries of each RyR monomer in a subnanomet resolution map of the RyR channel and to delineate the structure of each monomer in the cytoplasm and in the membrane.
the cytoplasm of the RyR1 tetramer is organized into distinct regions that are likely to be involved in channel gating.
the cytoplasmically exposed region of RyR1 is a complex structure with multiple domains and a large surface area that is accessible to other molecules.
